Music / Listening room

The lost pleasure of making someone a mixtape

A small collection of songs can say something a message cannot.

✳
The Offbeat EditCulture Issue · 2 min read

IN THIS STORY

Begin with a personEdit the middleGive it a proper endingMore from Music

Begin with a person

The best mix has a listener in mind. Think about a shared journey, a joke, or the energy your friend might want after a long day. A specific intention makes choosing easier than trying to collect every song you love.

Choose an opening track that invites attention without giving everything away. Then find a second song that creates a connection through rhythm, texture, or a lyric rather than simply repeating the same mood.

Edit the middle

A short mix gives every song a reason to be there. Listen to the transitions instead of checking titles on a screen. A moment of contrast can keep a sequence alive, especially after several songs with similar arrangements.

Remove anything that feels like homework. You are sharing an experience, not proving your taste. If a favourite track does not fit the journey, save it for another mix.

Give it a proper ending

An ending can settle the mood or send the listener somewhere unexpected. Try listening to the last two songs together before you call the mix finished.

Add a short note about why you made it. Share links through a licensed service, or make a list of titles and artists. The personal gesture matters more than the format.

“A small collection of songs can say something a message cannot.”
